# QS-CFW-7434-20 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (1045)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P2  
Parts: CFW-7434-20

## Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) manufactured from material grade 1045 at Plant P2. It applies to all finished forging deliveries and to in-process forgings proceeding to final machining at Plant P2. The intent is to control mechanical properties and critical dimensions that affect fit, performance, and service life.

Background and rationale: The connecting rod is a safety-critical rotating component. Hardness and bore control are primary determinants of wear life and fatigue performance after heat treatment and machining. Maximum forging weight governs lift and handling constraints for safe material flow and tooling limits. This document sets clear pass/fail criteria and inspection practices to ensure downstream machining and assembly stability.

## Requirements table

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Hardness (post-heat-treatment, finished) | The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC. | Within specified range: Accept. Outside specified range: Reject. |
| Bore diameter (as-forged / pre-machining) | The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.07 mm. | Within tolerance: Accept for machining. Outside tolerance: Reject for rework or scrap. |
| Forging mass | The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg. | Less than or equal to maximum: Accept for standard handling. Greater than maximum: Reject for lift review and containment. |

Notes:
- The hardness requirement applies to the measured surface or cross-section specified by the inspection method below. Hardness readings inconsistent with process capability shall trigger corrective action.
- Bore diameter tolerance applies to the diameter measured at the location and method defined in the inspection method. Feature control applies to pre-machining condition and informs machining allowances.
- Maximum forging weight is used to determine handling, tooling and transport limits. Forgings exceeding the stated maximum shall not proceed to normal handling flows.

## Inspection method

General principles: Use calibrated instruments and certified personnel for all inspections. Record the instrument identification and calibration status in the inspection record. Ensure surface cleanliness and representative sampling. Measurements must be taken at controlled locations described below and recorded verbatim.

Hardness inspection procedure:
- Condition: Inspect on the finished, heat-treated surface after any required tempering and prior to any final finish machining operations that would alter near-surface hardness.
- Method: Use an appropriate hardness tester and test block traceable to calibration standards. Take multiple measurements across the cross-section where representative hardness is required, avoiding obvious defects or scale. Ensure readings are stable before recording.
- Recording: Enter the measured values on the inspection record and compare to the requirement. If any recorded value is outside the hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC., mark the part as nonconforming and follow the nonconformance handling procedure.

Bore diameter inspection procedure:
- Condition: Inspect bores on the as-forged pre-machining component after any final forging cleanup but before machining that will alter bore size.
- Method: Use a calibrated dimensional measuring device appropriate for the bore geometry. Measure at locations specified in the part drawing and record the nominal dimension plus the bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is ±0.07 mm. Report measured values and indicate conformance to tolerance.
- Recording: All measured values and the instrument used must be documented on the inspection record. Parts found outside the bore diameter tolerance shall be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.

Forging weight verification:
- Condition: Verify forging mass at the first receiving operation after forging removal from the die area.
- Method: Use the facility lifting or weighing system with traceable calibration. Record the measured mass and compare to the maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 101.0 kg.
- Recording: Weighing results shall be logged on the process traveler and attached inspection paperwork. Forgings exceeding the maximum shall be held and tagged.

Examples and rationale:
- Example inspection record entry for hardness: "Measured hardness values at three locations: value A, value B, value C; all compared to the hardness range for connecting rod CFW-7434-20 (CFW-7434-20) is 26-30 HRC."
- Example inspection record entry for bore: "Nominal bore X.XXX mm; measured Y.YYY mm; tolerance applied ±0.07 mm; disposition: Accept." Use consistent notation and avoid rounding that obscures conformance decisions.

Records to keep:
- Hardness test printouts or digital logs with tester ID and calibration date.
- Dimensional measurement reports including instrument ID and calibration status.
- Weighing records and tags for material handling.
- Part identification and traveler showing inspection outcomes and signatures. Maintain records in the document control system and attach them to the batch lot for traceability.

## Nonconformance handling

Segregation and identification:
- Any part failing to meet the hardness requirement, bore diameter tolerance, or maximum forging weight requirement must be tagged and moved to the designated hold area. Markings must reference the characteristic failed and the inspection record number.

Disposition options:
- Rework may be considered only if a documented engineering evaluation supports a corrective process that restores the product to full conformance without compromising integrity. Rework steps and approvals must be documented on the disposition form.
- If rework is not feasible, parts shall be scrapped or returned to the supplier per internal scrap handling procedures.

Root cause and correction:
- For each nonconformance, perform a root cause analysis and implement corrective action appropriate to the finding. Actions may include equipment maintenance, process parameter review, tooling inspection, or retraining. Document actions taken and verify effectiveness before returning affected lots to production flow.

Escalation and customer notification:
- Notify responsible quality personnel immediately for any nonconformance that may affect delivery or safety. Maintain communication records and final disposition documentation in the batch file.

Records of nonconformance:
- Maintain the hold tag, inspection record, disposition form, root cause analysis, and corrective action verification with the part lot documentation. These records must be available for audit and for review during manufacturing release.

End of document.
